raw:
The Dodgers, back-to-back champions in 2024 and 2025, entered 2026 as heavy preseason favorites (roughly 25% implied odds), and I have no reliable information on how their season actually went or on the World Series result. Assuming they are a playoff team in late September, even the strongest team rarely exceeds about 20% to win it all given the randomness of the MLB postseason. Uncertainty about their seeding and health (a first-round bye versus a wild-card series) pulls the estimate slightly below that preseason figure. I therefore put them at about the level of a typical top postseason favorite.

Probability: 0.18

Katie Hobbs is the Democratic incumbent running in a Trump-midterm year, which historically favours the party out of the White House. Arizona remains a closely divided state, and polling I'm aware of through mid-2026 showed Hobbs with only a modest lead over the likely Republican field (Andy Biggs the probable nominee). My knowledge stops in June 2026, so I have no information on the general-election campaign or the result of the 3 November election, and I am forecasting from the pre-election picture. On that basis I rate Hobbs a clear but not overwhelming favourite.

Probability: 0.73

I can't check the Brent price as of August 20, 2026, so this estimate rests on my recollection of earlier 2026 rather than current quotes. As I recall it, Brent spiked above $100 in spring 2026 on the Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption, then eased toward the mid-$80s to $90s by early summer on ceasefire and peace-deal hopes. That leaves the $84.99 strike plausibly near the middle of the likely range for August 31, with a slight lean below it if the easing trend continued. With no firm price anchor and only seven trading days of volatility left, I put this close to a coin flip, slightly under.

Probability: 0.42

Missouri voters approved abortion rights 52–48 in 2024, and the 2026 midterm, held under a Republican president, should favour Democratic-leaning turnout, which helps the "No" side. Abortion-restricting measures have also failed in other red states such as Kansas and Kentucky in 2022. Against that, Missouri is solidly Republican, the measure is bundled with popular-sounding provisions (rape/incest exceptions, parental consent, a ban on gender-affirming care for minors), and it has the governor's backing. I have no reliable result or late polling to draw on, so this is a judgement from those fundamentals, leaning modestly towards the measure failing.

Probability: 0.38

"Blue tsunami" on Polymarket most likely means something stricter than a simple Democratic sweep, such as Democrats winning both the House and the Senate with sizeable margins; I can't check the exact resolution terms, so this is an assumption. As of my knowledge through mid-2026, Democrats were strong favourites to take the House but underdogs for the Senate, given a difficult map that required flipping several Republican-leaning seats. I don't have the actual election results, so I can't confirm the outcome either way. A sweep with a margin requirement on top of an already unlikely Senate flip puts this at a low probability.

Probability: 0.12

The Dodgers are the two-time defending champions with a deep roster, so they are likely among the favorites heading into the 2026 postseason. Even the strongest team entering October typically has only about a 15–25% chance of winning the title, because short playoff series are high-variance. I don't have reliable information on the final 2026 standings or the playoff bracket, so I can't justify moving far from that base rate. Your confidence doesn't change this: no single team is a strong favorite against the field before the playoffs start.

Probability: 0.18

Katie Hobbs is the Democratic incumbent, running in a midterm under a Republican president, which historically favors the out-party. Polling I'm aware of through mid-2026 showed her narrowly to modestly ahead of the likely Republican nominees, with a strong fundraising advantage. Arizona remains a closely divided state where Trump won by about 5.5 points in 2024, so a Republican win is still quite plausible. I don't have the actual election result, so this is a pre-election estimate, and your confidence doesn't change my read of the evidence.

Probability: 0.73

I don't have live price data for August 20, 2026, so I can't verify where Brent is trading relative to the 84.99 strike. My last solid recollection is that Brent was elevated in the first half of 2026 on Middle East supply disruption, but I'm unsure how much of that had unwound by late August. Kalshi usually sets strikes around the prevailing price, which suggests 84.99 is near the middle of the plausible range rather than a sure thing. Your confidence isn't something I can weigh without the reasoning or the current price behind it, so I'm staying near even odds.

Probability: 0.5
